details:
Separate the API from the instance hosting. Then add an instance browser.
I am very much in favor of EAC and think it will improve security against all the malicious things that have been floating around VRChat for years. When I saw that this was added, I had an idea that could benefit everyone even more and future proof things.
Separate the API from the instance hosting. Then add an instance browser. Now, instances running on VRChat servers, as they are now, need to run EAC in the background of everyone to connect to them. Other instances that are self-hosted can now choose to follow VRChat's TOS or the new "Instance TOS" and be added to the official instance browser list. Instances that do not follow VRChat's "Innstance TOS" must be manually added to the instance browser by anyone who wishes to connect to them.
Well, now you have EAC-protected official instances, then you have self-hosted EAC instances from community members, and you have non-official non-EAC instances. Everything that happens on these servers is not moderated by VRChat and is not directly visible to you. Anything that happens on these servers is not the problem of VRChat itself. Anyone who is hacked, scammed or whatever has chosen to join third-party instances that are not affiliated with VRChat. This has the potential to open VRChat up to not only its current content and assets, but anything 18+, or servers/instances for events and maybe even education, but of course also monetization.
Avatars, worlds & co. will still be hosted on VRChat unless you allow third-party sources. Assets hosted on third-party servers can only be accessed when you visit non-official instances that have EAC disabled.
Cons:
- This is very difficult to accomplish and would require a major redesign and overhaul of how API and instances are currently handled.
- People who do not use the official servers continue to use the traffic of the official API.
- This has the potential to divide large segments of the community.
Pros:
- Anyone using the official VRChat instances will continue to be kept safe and under moderation, even if modification use occurs on non-official instances alongside them.
- Some of the traffic and resources for the instances are moved to community-hosted servers.
- Users can now reach servers near them, as this allows them to host instances anywhere in the world.
- Anything that happens in non-official VRChat instances has nothing to do with VRChat and does not need to be moderated by them, that is now the hosts' job.
- Any user violating the Tos can still be banned from VRChat and loose their ability to join any instance, official or not.
- Any instance that violates VRChat's rules can be removed from the official instance browser at any time without having to deal with the host.
- Age-restricted content can now be completely removed from VRChat and moved to non-official servers. These servers might even opt for an age verification system.
This is probably the furthest "fetch" ever. I know this will never happen unless you, one of the team members, or even several reading this can see the future in this type of system. Think of Minecraft or Counter-Strike, Terraria or something similar, they do the exact same thing (Varies from game to game) for years. CS:GO even has exactly the anti-cheat method per instance that I just described. (VAC-protected servers and non-VAC-protected servers).
Just an Idea.
title: Separate VRChat's API From Instance Hosting And Allow Self-Hosted Instances & Assets.
